hub.headline: BRender (Blazing Render) was Argonaut Software's real-time 3D engine of the 1990s.
hub.next: The modern 64-bit path is being chosen with BlazingRenderer in view, since that fork already runs BRender on current PCs. Textured output in one test path of the period build still renders black and is not claimed as working.
hub.what_it_was: BRender drew real-time 3D scenes in software on DOS, Windows, PlayStation and OS/2. It shipped through the 1990s and was used in titles such as Carmageddon, FX Fighter and Microsoft 3D Movie Maker. A variant of the library from about May 1995 sits inside 3D Movie Maker.
hub.what_survives: The BRender v1.3.2 source (about November 1998, copyright 1998 Argonaut Software Limited) is public under the MIT licence at foone/BRender-v1.3.2, released with approval attributed to Argonaut's former CEO Jez San. The 3D Movie Maker variant is public too, and BlazingRender.net indexes the source releases and old SDKs. BlazingRenderer maintains a modernized 64-bit fork (version 1.4.0, MIT) with a portable C software rasteriser and SDL3 and OpenGL drivers. The archive rebuilt v1.3.2 from that source: its 21-step test ladder builds and passes in CI, and the restoration is published at HarperZ9/brender-archival.

name: Argonaut BRender
summary: Open BRender source releases and the public BRender Archival v0.1.1 restoration evidence are tracked as the first critical-edition revival lane.
